% clauses — a numbered clause hierarchy, read from the structure tree.
%
% One concern: does the tagged path reconstruct nesting from the tree rather than
% guessing it from type size? This is the only tagged fixture, and it is the one
% that matters most for the corpus: every ISO document we read is tagged, numbered,
% and nested three or four deep, and a clause attached to the wrong parent silently
% moves a whole subtree in the output.
%
% Numbered explicitly in the section titles rather than left to LaTeX's counters,
% because the number is part of the text a clause is identified by — the gold file
% has to assert "4.2.1 Nested subclause" as a string, and a counter that starts at
% a different value would change the assertion without changing the structure.
%
% Build this one with lualatex, not pdflatex. Two reasons, both measured:
%
% A kernel old enough to predate the latex-lab tagging code fails outright with
% \DebugTemplatesOff undefined, whichever engine runs it. That is a version skew and
% it announces itself.
%
% The second is quieter and is why the engine is named here rather than left to
% whatever is on the path. pdfTeX's tagging backend writes /MCID 1 into every one of
% this document's ten /MCR entries while the content stream draws 0 through 9, so
% nine of the ten structure elements join to nothing: the clause titles survive
% (they come from /T) and every body paragraph falls out of the tree into Unplaced.
% Extracting that build produced five headings with no bodies and a duplicate dump of
% the whole page. lualatex writes 0 through 9 and the same source extracts exactly.
%
% A reader has no way to tell that file from a document whose paragraphs genuinely
% are untagged, so it is the wrong yardstick — it would assert our behaviour on a
% broken producer instead of on a correct one. The committed PDF means a clone never
% builds either.
\DocumentMetadata{pdfstandard=ua-2, tagging=on}
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\pagestyle{empty}
\setcounter{secnumdepth}{0}
\begin{document}

\section{4 Clause four}

Body of clause four.

\subsection{4.1 First subclause}

Body of the first subclause.

\subsection{4.2 Second subclause}

Body of the second subclause.

\subsubsection{4.2.1 Nested subclause}

Body of the nested subclause.

\section{5 Clause five}

Body of clause five.

\end{document}
